scenarios.name: normal_operation
scenarios.description: The reference's published vector 1: pump commanded on, proven running, 3.2 L/s of flow. Well above the 1.0 L/s no-flow line, so the rule is live and silent. yRunOk is false only on the init tick, while the 60 s flow_check_delay rides out the start transient.

scenarios.name: no_flow_pump_running
scenarios.description: The reference's published vector 2: commanded on, proven running, zero flow. The run condition settles at exactly 60 s and the alarm lands at exactly 360 s — flow_check_delay plus alarm_delay, the two delays adding exactly.

scenarios.name: pump_off
scenarios.description: The reference's published vector 3: pump off, no flow, expected NO_EVAL. yRunOk is false for the whole run, which is how the host distinguishes this from a healthy pump — an idle pump makes no flow and that means nothing.

scenarios.name: flow_exactly_at_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary: flow sits exactly on no_flow_threshold (1.0 L/s). CDL Reals has no LessEqual, so the comparison is strict and exactly 1.0 is not 'no flow'.

scenarios.name: flow_just_below_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary from below: 0.9 L/s clears the strict comparison and alarms on the same 360 s schedule as zero flow.

scenarios.name: flow_just_above_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary from above: 1.1 L/s is flow, however little, and never alarms.

scenarios.name: commanded_on_but_not_running
scenarios.description: Commanded on with status false and zero flow. This is a real failure — a pump that will not start — and it is not this one: yRunOk is false, so the verdict is NO_EVAL rather than 'no flow detected'. No library rule covers it today (see Deviations).

scenarios.name: running_while_commanded_off
scenarios.description: The other mismatch: status true against a command of off, zero flow. A welded contactor or a hand-off-auto switch left in hand. Also NO_EVAL here — the reference's equation requires both conjuncts and this rule reports on neither mismatch.

scenarios.name: flow_in_the_deadhead_band
scenarios.description: 1.5 L/s: above this rule's 5%-of-design no-flow line and below PMP-FC-051's 10%-of-design deadhead line. Silent here by design; PMP-FC-051 is the rule that reports this band when the pump DP is also high.

scenarios.name: flow_lost_mid_run
scenarios.description: A pump running normally loses its flow at t=600 s. The run condition settled long ago, so only alarm_delay is left to run and the alarm lands at exactly 900 s. This is the vector that pins the structure: with flow_check_delay applied to the whole conjunction instead of to the run condition, the alarm would come at 960 s and this window would fail.

scenarios.name: intermittent_flow_never_alarms
scenarios.description: Flow alternating between zero and 3.2 L/s every 240 s — an air-locked pump that keeps catching prime, or a flow meter dropping out. No single no-flow episode reaches alarm_delay, so nothing ever fires. Persistence is not averaging: a pump delivering flow half the time is a real finding this rule cannot make.

scenarios.name: flow_returns_after_alarm
scenarios.description: Recovery: the alarm asserts at 360 s and the pump picks up flow at t=900 s. TrueDelay passes the falling edge with no delay, so yFault drops on that tick and the accumulated time is discarded.

scenarios.name: status_drops_after_alarm
scenarios.description: The evaluability release: an alarming pump loses its run status at t=900 s. yFault and yRunOk go false on the same tick and only the pair tells the host that the pump stopped rather than started delivering — the analogue of VFD-FC-050's command_drops_below_floor_after_alarm.

scenarios.name: pump_starts_dry_mid_run
scenarios.description: The pump starts at t=600 s into a system that never produces flow. yRunOk asserts at exactly 660 s (60 s after the rising edge) and yFault at exactly 960 s — mid-run edges carry the same exact arithmetic as the init case.
